title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Strix Halo (gfx1151): 17 → 47 tok/s — working MTP on ROCm, measurements, reproducible stack
body:
Sharing a measured, reproducible stack for **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp)** on **Strix Halo** (Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, 128 GB unified, ROCm 7.1) — including what we believe is the first working native MTP speculative decoding for this model on ROCm.

**Headline, single-stream decode on real coding workloads (UD-IQ4_XS, greedy):**

| tok/s | no speculation | full stack |
|---|---|---|
| file rewrite @ 8k ctx | 16.8 | **47.1** |
| new code @ 8k | 16.8 | **31.7** |
| file rewrite @ 24k | ~15 | **28.6** |
| new code @ 24k | ~15 | **25.4** |

The stack is three composable levers:

1. **GPU TOP_K** — the QSA indexer runs `ggml_top_k` over the whole context 12×/token, and stock HIP falls back to **CPU** past ne=1024 (no CUB). This is why qwen4exp decode collapses with depth on ROCm — the knee is at exactly d1024. Fixed by #26592 (hipCUB) or #27466 (native radix). +38–53% end-to-end at 24k.
2. **Native MTP** (#27836) + crusaderky's detached-head loader fix + a converter whitelist fix ([rmonsurate/llama.cpp#1](https://github.com/rmonsurate/llama.cpp/pull/1)). Output verified byte-clean at long prompts — an earlier community MTP port produced genuine-looking tok/s while emitting multilingual noise above ~1k prompt tokens, so *read the output, not just the counter*.
3. **ngram-mod** on top: `--spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod`.

**Everything packaged:**

- Guide with build/run lines and the pitfalls (llama-bench's `-ub 2048` trap, `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` on ROCm < 7.13 and why, dio vs mmap load, why fleet serving isn't worth it on this MoE): **https://github.com/drluoto/flash-next-strix-halo**
- Pre-assembled branch: [`drluoto/llama.cpp` → `strix-halo-flash-next`](https://github.com/drluoto/llama.cpp/tree/strix-halo-flash-next)
- ROCm-verified MTP sidecar from the official checkpoint: [drluoto/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MTP-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/drluoto/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MTP-GGUF)
- The head was extracted with HTTP range reads — 5.2 GB fetched instead of the 360 GB checkpoint: [shard-scalpel](https://github.com/drluoto/shard-scalpel)

Credits where due: rmonsurate (MTP), crusaderky (loader), Geramy (hipCUB + rocPRIM capture diagnosis), jadenmach2 (radix TOP_K), Unsloth (port + quants), JJJYmmm/Qwen (arch). Raw measurement data lives in the three PR threads. Happy to run follow-ups on this hardware.

nodes.body:
Small find that ended up mattering more than any kernel work this week.

My agent shares one llama-server with cron jobs and delegations. One slot = every session evicts the other's cache. Coming back to the main chat meant 1.5–4 min of re-prefill at ~30k ctx. That is what "slow" actually felt like — not decode.

Fix: `-np 3 --ctx-checkpoints 8`. The server already routes each request to the most similar slot (LCP matching), so every session keeps its own warm cache. Return TTFT on real traces: 21–251 s → **0.3–0.5 s**. No code.

Two things worth knowing:

- Checkpoints are mandatory on this arch. 36 recurrent GDN layers can't roll back without them.
- Slot save/restore to disk is NOT a working alternative here. Restore returns OK, the server even logs `f_sim_best = 1.000` — and then re-prefills from zero anyway, because the recurrent checkpoint stack isn't part of the saved state. Cost me an evening.

Extra slots are ~free as long as turns are sequential. Concurrent streams are a different story on this MoE (see up-thread).

Detached MTP sidecar fails to load on strix-halo-flash-next (gfx1151, ROCm 10.0)

Trying to reproduce your stack. The TOP_K side works, but the detached -md sidecar does not load — including when loaded on its own, so it is not a target-pairing issue.

Setup: drluoto/llama.cpp@strix-halo-flash-next (590ac45), built with -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151, ROCm 10.0, Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S, 96 GB unified. Sidecar is your own drluoto/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MTP-GGUF/mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0.gguf.

The file's metadata looks right:

general.architecture = qwen4exp
qwen4exp.block_count = 49
qwen4exp.nextn_predict_layers = 1
37 tensors, head at blk.48.*  (output_hc_norm/down/up present at model level)

Loading it alone (llama-server -m <sidecar> -c 512 -lv 5):

kv 22: qwen4exp.nextn_predict_layers u32 = 1
print_info: n_layer     = 49
print_info: n_layer_all = 49
create_tensor: loading tensor blk.0.hc_attn_norm.weight
error loading model: check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.0.hc_attn_norm.weight' not found

n_layer should be 48 (n_layer_all - n_layer_nextn), so n_layer_nextn appears to be 0 at that point despite the KV being read. That would make mtp_only false in qwen4exp.cpp:160, leave trunk_flags at 0, and make the layer loop at :204 demand the full trunk — which matches the failure exactly. 


Happy to run anything you want checked on this box.

**Another data point — Vulkan backend, ROCmFP4-FAST quant, 46.9 t/s decode at 24k ctx**

Sharing our stack since this thread helped us get there. Notable: we hit these numbers on the **Vulkan** backend (not HIP), with the ROCmFP4-FAST weight format from @charlie12345's ROCmFPX — the FP4-FAST quants run fine through the Vulkan shader path on the same iGPU.

**Hardware/stack**
- Strix Halo 128GB (Ryzen AI Max+ 395 class, gfx1151), Fedora 44, 124GB GTT (`amdgpu.gttsize=126976` + `ttm.pages_limit=32505856`)
- llama.cpp b10981 (fork: LaurentZuijdwijk's qwen4exp MTP-draft work merged with upstream master incl. the ROCmFPX encoder fixes)
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Q4_0_ROCMFP4_FAST, ~90 GiB across 5 shards + 2.4 GiB MTP draft head
- CPU backend + Vulkan backend compiled in (no HIP/ROCm backend in the build)

**Serve flags that matter** (everything else is standard)
```
-c 524288 -fa 1 --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 -np 2 \
--load-mode mmap -ngl 99 --jinja \
--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-adaptive \
--spec-draft-n-min 2 --spec-draft-n-max 4 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 \
--spec-draft-model <MTP-ROCmFP4-FAST.gguf>
```

**Numbers** (same-session A/B, medians of 2 reps per size, bench through llama-server with production flags since `llama-bench` can't see draft flags)

| context | tg before | tg after | pp |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~24k (large) | 40.0 | **46.9** | ~192 |
| med | 28.4 | 29.8 | ~55 |
| small | 36.4 | 31.9 | ~56 |

MTP draft acceptance 0.86–1.00 across all bench traffic (server-side `print_timing` telemetry), mean draft len ~4.

The large-context gain came with the merge that picked up the ROCmFPX encoder fixes + 80 upstream commits (b10951→b10981), so I can't attribute it cleanly — but the before/after is same-session, same-flags.

**Two things we learned the hard way:**

1. **Same-build noise is huge — don't trust single-run posts (including screenshots).** The *same binary* measured 25–36 t/s on identical med-context rows across two days. We now bench A/B in the same session and compare row-level spread before believing any delta. Whatever you post, post both legs.

2. **Merging a qwen4exp fork with upstream: watch the `n_ff_exp` API break.** Upstream changed `hparams.n_ff_exp` (member) to `hparams.n_ff_exp(il)` (function). Fork MTP-draft/tensor-split code that uses the member form compiles into a runtime assert (`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->ne[axis] == 2*n_ff_exp)` paths in `llama-model.cpp`). Grep for `n_ff_exp` at the compile gate — member form without a call = stale.

Minor: if you're driving this model from agentic loops, `enable_thinking: false` via `chat_template_kwargs` cuts time-to-first-byte roughly 3x (~4.3s → ~1.3s) with no quality loss for routing/judging tasks.

Full replication config — kernel cmdline, systemd units, bench harness, and the raw jsonl ledgers from this box: https://github.com/KYmidnight/strix-halo-qwen38-flash
